## Measured Quality Bands

Department scores measured from the generated first-choice eleven of a real
club, through the production team-strength path. The `reference` band is the
median first-division club flattened to one uniform value, so that every
structural comparison has a single unambiguous quality number.

These bands hold for a **single-country population**. With five countries,
`first division` and `third division` stop denoting one quality scale and
every band below must be re-derived rather than carried over.

## Department Collapse

The reachable population is 66 department compositions, which the current
engine reduces to **7 distinct team strengths**. Every composition that
populates all four departments produces byte-identical strength, because
`deriveTeamStrength` averages inside a department and therefore cannot see how
many slots are in it. The only structural signal the engine has today is
whether a department is *empty*.

## Tactic Profiles At The Reference Shape

Each profile moves one knob to its extreme against the same shape playing the
neutral tactic, so whatever moves belongs to that knob. `neutral` plays itself
and its win share is the measurement's own noise reading.

Chance types come from a deterministic texture rather than from a route today.
They are recorded as the thing Step 06 replaces, not as evidence that routes
already exist.

is worth in win share at identical shape. The bounded-swing invariant compares
the best structural gain against it.

## Frozen Invariants

Thresholds were fixed before any behaviour change and are never re-derived
from output. `not_evaluated` is never reported as a pass.

| Invariant | Status | Observed | Observations | Frozen threshold |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bounded_structural_swing` | PASS | 0.169 | 1600 | best shape's gain over the reference shape <= 0.75 x the division-tier edge |
| `no_dominant_composition` | PASS | 0.375 | 35376 | no composition stays above 0.55 against every single opponent |
| `asymmetric_incoherence_cost` | not_evaluated | - | 0 | worst-shape deficit / best-shape surplus >= 2, both measured against the reference shape |
| `quality_hierarchy_survives_extreme_shape` | PASS | 0.925 | 800 | contender win share >= 0.55 with at least 1 upset |
| `empty_department_possession_clamp` | PASS | 0.18 | 66 | every recorded possession share stays inside [0.18, 0.82] and every empty-midfield shape sits on the floor |
| `distinguishable_coherent_and_incoherent_shape` | not_evaluated | 7 | 66 | equal-quality 4-4-2 and 3-1-6 must produce different team strength; owned by Step 03 and enforced from Step 06 |

- `bounded_structural_swing`: The best shape against the reference is 1-6-3 at 0.5431, worth 0.0431 win share, against a division-tier edge of 0.255. Downside is deliberately unbounded: a manager who fields a self-destructive shape may lose as much as the engine says.
- `no_dominant_composition`: The nearest thing to a dominant shape is 1-4-5, which still drops to 0.375 against its worst matchup while averaging 0.6714 against the whole population.
- `asymmetric_incoherence_cost`: The best shape gains 0.0431 over the reference, which is inside the measurement noise floor 0.0477. There is no coherence reward to compare against, so the ratio is undefined rather than satisfied (largest deficit 0.4769 from 0-0-10).
- `quality_hierarchy_survives_extreme_shape`: First-division contender using 3-1-6 held 0.925 win share over third-division 4-4-2 across 800 matches with 30 upsets
- `empty_department_possession_clamp`: All 11 empty-midfield shapes sat on the 0.18 floor against 4-4-2, 2-0-8 among them at 0.18 share, and every other recorded share stayed inside the clamp
- `distinguishable_coherent_and_incoherent_shape`: Step 01 changes no behaviour, so this invariant records the starting point instead of passing: 7 distinct strength fingerprints across 66 reachable compositions. Step 03 introduces intrinsic shape and Step 06 is the first step that can satisfy this gate.
